questions.question_text: Which unit is most appropriate for the mass of a paper clip?

options.why: Uses an everyday-object unit that is too large for one paper clip.
Uses a unit for extremely heavy loads instead of a light object.

questions.solution_text:
A paper clip is light, so its mass is measured in grams.
$\text{Unit}=\text{g}$

questions.question_text: Which unit is most appropriate for the mass of a motorbike?

options.why: Uses a unit suited to light objects, making the numerical mass impractically large.
Uses a unit suited to much heavier vehicles and loads than one motorbike.

questions.solution_text:
A motorbike has a mass of hundreds of kilograms.
$\text{Unit}=\text{kg}$

questions.question_text: Which unit is most appropriate for the mass of a passenger ferry?

options.why: Uses an everyday mass unit instead of the practical unit for a very heavy vessel.
Uses a unit for light objects, which is unsuitable for a large vessel.

questions.solution_text:
A passenger ferry is very heavy, so tonnes are appropriate.
$\text{Unit}=\text{t}$

questions.question_text: Which device should a café use to measure $24\text{ g}$ of coffee beans?

options.why: Chooses scales designed for body masses, not small ingredient masses.
Chooses a device for vehicles and loads measured in tonnes.

questions.solution_text:
A small ingredient mass needs kitchen scales that read grams.
Use **digital kitchen scales**.

questions.question_text:
A zookeeper needs the mass of an elephant before transport.
Which pair is most sensible?

options.why: Chooses a device and unit whose capacity suits food, not an elephant.
Chooses a device whose capacity is far below an elephant's mass.

questions.solution_text:
An elephant is very heavy and needs high-capacity platform scales.
Use **platform scales and tonnes**.

questions.question_text:
A small bag of flour is listed as having a mass of $500\text{ kg}$.
Which correction is most reasonable?

options.why: Changes to an even larger unit used for vehicles and heavy loads.
Keeps the unreasonable unit that would make one tablet heavier than a person.

questions.solution_text:
A small bag of flour has a mass of hundreds of grams, not hundreds of kilograms.
The reasonable correction is $500\text{ g}$.
